evals.name: readme only is not docs complete
evals.prompt: Use the documentation-boundary skill. A command-line flag changed behavior. The proposed update edits only README.md with a short mention and then claims documentation is complete. Review the plan.
evals.expected_output: The response rejects claiming documentation is complete from README-only changes. It treats README as a synopsis and requires updating the real documentation surface for the behavior change, such as docs, CLI help, man pages, or info pages when present, or explicitly explaining why none applies.
assertions: The output rejects or flags the claim that documentation is complete from only a `README.md` edit.
The output says `README.md` is a synopsis rather than the full documentation.
The output requires updating a real documentation surface for the behavior change, such as `docs/`, CLI help, man pages, or info pages when present.
The output allows no real documentation update only with an explicit reason.
The output requires reporting which documentation surfaces changed.

evals.name: report documentation surfaces
evals.prompt: Use the documentation-boundary skill. You changed docs/development/local-dev.md, updated README.md links, and did not change CLI help, man pages, info pages, or changelog prose. State the documentation boundary report.
evals.expected_output: The response reports README synopsis and docs changed, and explicitly reports that CLI help, man or info pages, and changelog did not change. It does not imply the README edit alone was the documentation update.
assertions: The output reports that the README synopsis changed.
The output reports that `docs/` changed.
The output reports that CLI help did not change.
The output reports that man or info pages did not change.
The output reports that changelog prose did not change.
The output does not claim the README edit alone was the full documentation update.

evals.name: reject README as manual
evals.prompt: Use the documentation-boundary skill. Review this documentation change before I commit it: I copied the deployment guide, troubleshooting catalog, full command reference, and failure-drill runbook into README.md so users can find everything from the repository front page. The original docs files still exist.
evals.expected_output: The response rejects or flags the README expansion. It treats README.md as a synopsis rather than the full documentation, keeps only concise entry-point material there, and sends durable deployment, troubleshooting, command reference, and runbook content back to docs, CLI help, man pages, info pages, or dedicated references. It reports that README synopsis and docs changed, and does not claim README alone is the real documentation.
assertions: The output rejects or flags copying the deployment guide, troubleshooting catalog, command reference, and failure-drill runbook into README.md.
The output says README.md should remain a synopsis, quick entry point, or short overview rather than the full documentation.
The output moves long procedural detail, troubleshooting, deployment detail, command reference, or failure drills to docs, help text, man pages, info pages, or dedicated references.
The output preserves essential first-run or relevance information in README rather than removing README usefulness entirely.
The output reports which documentation surfaces changed, including README synopsis and docs.

evals.name: require CLI help for CLI behavior
evals.prompt: Use the documentation-boundary skill. Review this release note before I close the task: the `cache clean --stale` flag now marks entries for delayed cleanup instead of deleting them immediately. I updated docs/cache.md and CHANGELOG.md. The command has built-in help and a man page, but I did not touch them.
evals.expected_output: The response rejects closing the task as documented. It requires updating the relevant CLI help and man page because the CLI behavior changed and those surfaces exist. It treats docs/cache.md and the changelog as insufficient by themselves, and reports docs and changelog changed while CLI help and man pages still need changes.
assertions: The output rejects or flags closing the task as fully documented.
The output requires updating the command's `--help` text for the changed flag behavior.
The output requires updating the man page because it exists and describes the command behavior.
The output does not treat `docs/cache.md` alone as enough for the CLI behavior change.
The output reports that docs and changelog changed while CLI help and man pages still need changes.

evals.name: reject changelog as docs
evals.prompt: Use the documentation-boundary skill. Review this plan before implementation: the next release introduces a new config file format and users must migrate existing projects. I plan to put the migration instructions in CHANGELOG.md and the release notes only, because people read those during upgrades.
evals.expected_output: The response rejects relying on changelog prose or release notes as the real documentation update. It says migration behavior needs an appropriate documentation surface such as docs, CLI help, README links, man pages, or info pages when relevant. It may keep the changelog entry as release history, but requires real documentation or an explicit no-surface rationale, and reports changelog changed while docs and other documentation surfaces still need attention.
assertions: The output rejects or flags relying only on CHANGELOG.md or release notes for the migration behavior change.
The output says changelog prose or release notes are not the real documentation surface for changed behavior.
The output requires an appropriate documentation surface such as docs, CLI help, README links, man pages, or info pages when relevant.
The output allows the changelog entry to remain as release history without counting it as sufficient documentation.
The output reports that changelog prose changed while docs or other real documentation surfaces still need attention.

evals.name: do not overrequire docs for docs-only maintenance
evals.prompt: Use the documentation-boundary skill. Review this closeout note: I fixed broken README.md links, shortened duplicated README prose, and adjusted docs/index.md navigation labels. The checklist template says every change needs docs, CLI help, man page, and changelog updates before closure.
evals.expected_output: The response does not require additional feature documentation because this is docs-only maintenance with no behavior change. It reports README synopsis and docs changed, and reports that CLI help, man or info pages, and changelog did not change. It distinguishes docs-only maintenance from behavior changes that require real documentation surfaces.
assertions: The output says no additional feature or behavior documentation is required for this docs-only maintenance.
The output rejects or narrows the checklist template's claim that CLI help, man page, and changelog updates are always required.
The output reports that the README synopsis changed.
The output reports that docs changed.
The output reports that CLI help did not change.
The output reports that man or info pages and changelog prose did not change.
